rationale: Evidence: iteration 1 (sensors at x=-0.03..+0.03, 16 mm footprints, kp 1.5, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.4) raised the development score from 26.0 to 52.8, but every run still went off track with one line-loss event each. max_error is 0.061 to 0.065 m against a 0.06 m limit, and rms_error stayed near 0.03 m. The failure is therefore a transient right after the line is lost, not steady drift. Iteration 1 mixed results: the oval improved slightly (0.0606 vs 0.0614), but the s-bend (0.0639 vs 0.0611) and slalom (0.065 vs 0.0609) got worse. Lowering kp weakened the steering authority at the edge. When only the outer sensor sees tape, the signal is about +/-2, so turn is about kp*2. At kp 1.5 that is roughly 1050 PWM of wheel difference, which is too weak to pull the robot back before it reaches 0.05 m, where the line is lost. Changes: (a) kp raised from 1.5 back to 2.0 to restore edge steering authority; (b) kd raised from 0.1 to 0.15 to damp the faster response and limit overshoot after recovery; (c) base_speed held at 1.4 so that speed is not changed at the same time as the gains, which keeps the effect of this iteration interpretable; (d) sensor geometry kept at 16 mm footprints and x=-0.03..+0.03, since it is the best-scoring geometry so far. line_loss stays last_direction. Expected result: fewer or shorter line-loss transients, max_error near or below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend, and a clean run that may still stop short of progress 0.995 at this speed. Hypotheses to check: (1) if max_error drops below 0.06 with line_loss_events 0 or 1, the gain change was the fix and speed can rise to about 1.6; (2) if steering_oscillation rises sharply (above about 0.2) with kd 0.15, kd was too high and should return to about 0.1; (3) if line_loss_events stays at 1 on every track, the limit is the sensor reach (line lost near 0.05 m offset), and a wider sensor spread or a different line_loss mode (search_right) is the next test.
